mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months (FEDFUNDS decreasing from previous month) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the past 3 months (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL MoM increase > 0.2%) signals an expansionary economic phase with accommodative policy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting both conditions (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In high housing market activity (HOUST > 950 thousand units), a rising industrial production (INDPRO MoM increase > 0.5%) signals robust manufacturing and consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 950 and INDPRO MoM increase > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market indicated by non-farm payrolls above 138,000 thousand persons supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS > 138000 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO MoM increase > 0.5%) signals robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO MoM increase > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong economic growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2.0%) and rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL MoM increase > 0.2%) signals a robust economy with pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting both conditions (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: During low inflation (CPIAUCSL MoM increase < 0.1%), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS MoM increase > 0.1%) signals monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL MoM increase < 0.1% and FEDFUNDS MoM increase > 0.1% (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).
